title: Meet the 555
brief: A chip is a whole circuit in a package, and it does nothing until it's powered. The 555 straddles the channel, notch to the left: pin 1 bottom-left, counting right along the bottom, then back along the top.
Power: pin 8 (VCC) to +, pin 1 (GND) to −. Pin 4 (RESET) to + as well, or the chip stays switched off.
Pin 2 (TRIGGER) to −: that says 'output on'. Pin 6 (THRESHOLD) to − too, for now. Pin 3 is the output: through a resistor to the LED.
lesson: Inside the 555 is a switch with three inputs: TRIGGER low turns it on, THRESHOLD high turns it off, RESET low overrides both. Levels 8–10 use each of them.
